item.title: Why I Use Podman over Docker
item.description:
If you ever start self-hosting, there is a very good chance you will be encouraged to use containers. That’s for good reason. In general, it is better to containerize something if you can. Containers are kind of like a miniature VM: It makes sure dependencies run smoothly without having to worry about different Containers messing each other’s files.

Docker is usually the go-to tool for this but I recommend people to just go to Podman. I have started with Docker and even appreciated Docker Compose but there are several reasons I decided to move.

item.title: Software Minimalism
item.description:
In my journey to become a minimalist, one of the things that I fail to apply the knowledge to is Software. But as my relationship with technology has evolved, I realized it is something that needs culling.

Earlier this year, I downgraded my phone from an iPhone 14 Pro Max to a Samsung A56 5G. That said, I cannot really call it a downgrade in a traditional sense since I just moved into a phone that actually served my needs.

item.title: Please use ISO 8601 for your dates in files
item.description:
tl;dr: When you need to state the date, just use YYYY-MM-DD.

ISO 8601 is pretty simple: Date is YYYY-MM-DD and time is HH:MM. Please use it. Benefits include:

  1. Automatic sorting through names. I don’t get how people are NOT annoyed with Jan appearing after Apr in their file lists. Stop. Just use 2026-01-01 and you will always see it before 2026-04-01 unless you sort by other means. 2. Understandable by anyone. 02-12-2026 can either mean February 12 or December 2. Stop the confusion and use either 2026-12-02 or 2026-02-12. 3. Automatic versioning. If you add hours and minutes (even as HH-MM), it’s not that hard to think of the next version because you can just use the time you save the file.

Before people tell me that the date is in the metadata, I would really like to say that zipping it or uploading it somewhere can change it. Not to mention a random stray save can ruin your day.

item.title: My Self Hosting Journey after ~18 months
item.description: It’s been around a year and a half since I started self hosting. It all started when I bought a Raspberry Pi for no good reason. I installed a few apps before succumbing to compute limits. At times, it would randomly shut down because it could not get enough power. I cannot even plug an HDD as it would pull too much power. I bought a used Dell Optiplex from a second-hand seller. I think it was a company pull-out which was fine as I got it for just ~1000 PHP. I then upgraded the SSD and the RAM which took ~9000 PHP (this was before the RAMpocalypse and the SSD shortage). And now, for a year, it is going very smoothly.
